raw_findings.message: Adjacency-based movement allows `done` tasks to move back to `review`, although `NEXT_STATUSES` advertises only `archived` as an allowed next status for `done`.
`parseInt` accepts numeric prefixes and returns `NaN` for nonnumeric input, while both range comparisons let those values through, so priorities such as `2junk` or `foo` are stored as invalid values.
Spreading the unfiltered patch lets an owner overwrite protected fields such as `ownerId`, `status`, or `id`, enabling ownership changes and workflow bypasses through PATCH.
When no task has the requested ID, `find` returns `undefined` and dereferencing `task.status` throws instead of returning a not-found response.
Default array sorting compares numeric IDs as strings, so a column containing IDs 1, 2, and 10 is returned in the order 1, 10, 2 instead of oldest-first order.
An empty board has zero active tasks, so completion becomes `NaN` and is serialized as `null` rather than a valid percentage.
The user-controlled search query is compiled directly as a regular expression, allowing pathological patterns to trigger excessive backtracking or malformed patterns to throw.
The slice end subtracts one from the requested size, so every page returns one fewer result than requested and a size of one returns no results.
Task titles are interpolated into an HTML fragment without escaping, so a title containing markup or script executes when search results are rendered.
Request chunks are buffered without a size limit, allowing a client to exhaust server memory by sending an excessively large body.
Unexpected errors are returned with their stack traces and messages, exposing server implementation details to clients when an error occurs.
The server treats the client-supplied `X-User` header as authenticated identity, so a caller can impersonate a task owner and pass the owner check.
